rationale: Eighty-third pass: correct an overreach found by comparing two accounts that had grown apart. The snapshot-save question treats a hard save error as ending the process, and that termination is what keeps a failed save from stranding the saving flag. The worker-panic question records that the same termination depends on the launcher supplied by the pinned dependency, which is outside the captured snapshot. The behavior entry behind both statements still asserts termination as a target fact. This pass narrows the entry to what the target supports - the panic leaves the worker function and nothing in the target recovers it - names the launcher as the unresolved link, and reopens the save question's gap, because if the launcher recovered the panic the node would keep running with the saving flag set, the apply loop would skip the cluster and the periodic snapshot duty would be silently lost, which is the defect the earlier account had refuted. No new evidence is claimed; the measurement of the save-error path is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: A non-soft error returned by node.save is raised as a panic inside the snapshot worker: ssWorker.save calls panic(err) when node.save returns an error, and neither workerMain nor handle installs a recover, so the panic leaves the worker function. The only recover in engine.go is installed around step workers when error injection is enabled, and NodeHost.Start's recover wraps only the body of Start and re-panics through panicNow for error values, so no recover inside the captured target converts a runtime snapshot save error into a node-level or cluster-level result. Whether that panic then ends the process or only the goroutine depends on the launcher the syncutil stopper uses in the pinned goutils dependency, which is not part of the captured snapshot, so the target supports the propagation out of the worker but not the outcome after it.
knowledge.conditions: A snapshot save task is executed by the snapshot worker pool, and node.doSave returns an error other than the abort-class and soft errors it handles internally; the goroutine launcher comes from the pinned dependency and is outside the snapshot.
knowledge.changed_premise: The termination half of the earlier statement exceeded the captured evidence. The worker goroutine is launched by dependency code, so the entry now stops at 'the panic leaves the worker function', keeps only the recovers that exist inside the target, and names the launcher as the unresolved link.

interpretations.rationale: Current claim: the control flow around a periodic snapshot save is traced and the non-fatal outcomes are settled, but the conclusion that a hard save error cannot strand the snapshot duty depends on a link the captured target does not contain, so the claim is now conditional and the defect judgment is withdrawn. Basis: (1) saveSnapshotRequired advances the requested snapshot index only when it actually requests a snapshot, and it suppresses further periodic requests while the node reports itself busy snapshotting, so the requested index alone cannot suppress later attempts. (2) On every non-fatal path node.save returns nil, node.saveDone stores a completed save task through notifySnapshotStatus and signals the apply worker, and the apply worker's processStatusTransition calls processSaveStatus, which clears the saving flag before handling the next task; this covers the soft-error and abort-class returns and does not depend on any launcher. (3) A hard error is different: ssWorker.save calls panic(err) and neither the worker body nor anything else in the target recovers it, so the panic leaves the worker function. What happens next is decided by the launcher the syncutil stopper supplies from the pinned goutils dependency, which is not part of the captured snapshot. (4) The two outcomes differ in consequence, which is why the conclusion cannot stay refuted. If the launcher lets the panic end the process, the node never runs with a stale saving flag, as the earlier account argued. If it recovers the panic and only that goroutine dies, the process keeps running with the saving flag set: processSaveStatus would report the cluster busy on every pass, the apply loop would skip the cluster's tasks, and the periodic snapshot duty would be silently lost while entries keep committing - exactly the stranding this question originally suspected. (5) The evidence does not choose between those outcomes, so the earlier refutation is withdrawn and the question remains open pending the launcher behavior.

The panic itself and the absence of any recover inside the target are established, but the launcher that decides whether the process ends is dependency code outside the captured snapshot. Under the terminating outcome the node cannot continue with the saving flag set; under a recovering launcher it would keep running with the flag set, the apply loop would keep skipping that cluster, and later periodic snapshots would stay suppressed. The gap is therefore unresolved until the launcher behavior is established.
